summary: Arbitrary-base realization of the ordered pointed curve moduli problem: finite-stage models, cohomological genus and the log dualizing line, native groupoid-valued reindexing, polarized effective descent and the represented universal family. Existing parent identifiers and MC.2 sample suppliers are retained.

nodes.title: Finite-stage models of pointed curve diagrams
nodes.statement: Let A be a filtered colimit of finite-type Z-algebras A_i. Any finite diagram over Spec A of proper, flat, finitely presented, geometrically connected nodal curves of pure relative dimension one, equipped with finitely many ordered pairwise disjoint sections in the relative smooth locus and a fixed fibre genus for each curve, descends to some Spec A_i. Specified maps, isomorphisms, inverses, and finitely many commutative diagrams descend after a common refinement. Smoothness of a specified family and stability of a specified pointed family descend after refinement. The latter means positivity of 2h_v−2+b_v+m_v for every normalized geometric component, where b_v counts node branches. Two such finite-stage realizations of the same finite diagram become isomorphic at a common later stage, compatibly with all specified identifications. This is a local-on-the-base approximation theorem; it asserts no single Noetherian model for a non-quasi-compact base.
hypotheses: Every curve morphism is of finite presentation; only a finite diagram and finitely many marked sections are being descended.
The A_i form a filtered system of finite-type Z-algebras with colimit A.
Fixed genus, nonempty geometrically connected fibres, and pure relative dimension one are part of the objects.
proofSteps: Import SF.0/noetherian-approximation and SF.0/finite-presentation-limits for schemes, arrows, equalities and inverse equations. Spread properness and flatness after refining.

Apply Stacks Lemma 53.20.10 to spread nodality, using its syntomic relative-dimension-one and unramified-singular-locus criterion. Spread geometric connectedness using the SF.0 property-spreading contract; use the locally Noetherian genus strata from StableReduction Layer 2 to select genus g.

Over a Noetherian model, the failure loci for smooth marked sections, disjointness, smooth fibres and stable fibres are closed after taking the appropriate proper images. Remove their images and refine the model until the limit base factors through the resulting open. Fixed-genus strata are open and closed.

Apply the finite-presentation limit theorem again to comparisons and all finite relations. Apply the construction on affine opens of a general base and compare on affine refinements of their intersections; do not assume intersections or the base are quasi-compact.
acceptance: A marking permutation is a separately specified arrow, not an equality of ordered markings.
Nilpotents of the base are retained by scheme approximation.
No bound on the number of affine opens of an arbitrary base is imposed.

sources.match: Finite-presentation objects, arrows and equalities admit finite-stage models; ampleness can be detected at a later stage.
Nodality is described by finitely presented local conditions, is fpqc local and spreads through affine-transition limits.
The curve, section and fibrewise stability conditions being spread are those of the pointed moduli problem.

nodes.title: Genus and cohomology over arbitrary bases
nodes.statement: For a proper flat finitely presented scheme morphism f:C→S with nonempty geometrically connected nodal fibres of pure dimension one, the unit O_S→f_*O_C is an isomorphism universally; R¹f_*O_C is finite locally free, commutes with arbitrary base change, and R^qf_*O_C vanishes for q≥2. The geometric-fibre equality dim H¹(C_s,O)=g is equivalent to R¹f_*O_C having constant rank g. Formation of the genus-g open-and-closed locus commutes with arbitrary base change. On a locally Noetherian base this identifies with the genus convention and coherent cohomology of StableReduction Layer 2; over an affine base its groups identify with Tau Ceti scheme-module sheaf cohomology. No canonical splitting of Rf_*O_C is asserted.
hypotheses: S is any scheme, including nonreduced and non-Noetherian schemes.
Geometric connectedness, reduced nodal fibres, properness, flatness and finite presentation are essential hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the requested SF.2 perfect-pushforward theorem with E=O_C to obtain a perfect complex whose derived formation commutes with arbitrary base change.

Use geometric connectedness and geometric reducedness to identify fibre H⁰ with the residue field. The unit then gives a local splitting as in Stacks 36.32.5. Fibre dimension one eliminates cohomology in degrees ≥2.

Apply the requested perfect-complex fibre-amplitude criterion to the complementary complex, whose fibres are concentrated in degree one. Its degree-one cohomology is finite locally free and has arbitrary base change.
Identify affine sections using SF.2/qcoh-higher-direct-images and Tau Ceti Cohomology; compare with the Noetherian supplier using pointed-approximation and uniqueness of base-change identifications.
acceptance: For P¹_S, R¹f_*O=0 and the genus is zero.
For a smooth elliptic family the first cohomology has rank one, including after a nonflat change of base.
Two disjoint copies of P¹ fail the unit-isomorphism assertion: f_*O is O_S⊕O_S.

sources.match: A proper geometrically connected nodal family has universal degree-zero comparison, finite locally free first cohomology and higher vanishing.
Perfect pushforward and arbitrary base change yield the cohomological argument, with a local splitting rather than a distinguished one.
These identify the constant-genus locus by the rank of first cohomology.

nodes.title: Log dualizing sheaves over arbitrary bases
nodes.statement: For a proper flat finitely presented nodal curve f:C→S of pure relative dimension one over any scheme S, take the canonical relative dualizing complex supplied by SF.2/relative-dualizing-complex, with its diagonal rigidity and, for proper f, trace normalization. It is concentrated in degree −1, with cohomology ω_{C/S}; ω is an invertible O_C-module. For ordered disjoint smooth sections σ_i, their images are relative effective Cartier divisors D_i. Define L=ω_{C/S}(ΣD_i) using the existing invertible-sheaf tensor and Cartier-twist operations. Canonical comparisons u_C^*ω_{C/S}≅ω_{C_T/T} and u_C^*L≅L_T hold for every T→S, respect isomorphisms of pointed curves, and satisfy unit and composition coherence. On the locally Noetherian domain these identify with StableReduction Layer 2, including trace and smooth differential comparisons. On a geometric normalized component v, deg L=2h_v−2+b_v+m_v; a self-node contributes two to b_v. L is relatively ample exactly when all these degrees are positive. This extends the existing curve-specific dualizing interface; it does not introduce another line-bundle or generic duality theory.
hypotheses: Nodal fibres are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced; all geometric components have dimension one.
Each σ_i is a section in the relative smooth locus and the sections are pairwise disjoint.
For ampleness the morphism is proper and of finite presentation; no Noetherian condition is imposed on S.
proofSteps: Import the arbitrary-base rigid dualizing complex from SF.2. Use the requested arbitrary-base Cohen–Macaulay concentration and Gorenstein-invertibility extension to obtain its degree −1 module, with arbitrary base change.

Import relative Cartier marking divisors and log twists from StableReduction Layers 2–3. Form their tensor product with ω using the line-bundle API already owned by AlgebraicVectorBundles; do not replan those operations.

Compare with SF.2/curve-dualizing-comparison and the existing StableReduction sheaf on Noetherian models. Trace/rigidity uniqueness makes the comparisons independent of models and coherent; pointed-approximation handles finite diagrams.

Import the normalization residue and degree formula and componentwise positivity from StableReduction Layers 1–3. Reduce the fibrewise calculation to the Noetherian case; apply the relative ampleness criterion locally on S.
acceptance: P¹ with three distinct markings has L≅O(1), whereas two markings give O(0) and fail stability.
On two rational components joined at one node, each carrying two markings, L has multidegree (1,1).
A rational irreducible one-nodal curve with one smooth mark has degree one: the self-node has two branches.

sources.match: For arbitrary-base Cohen–Macaulay curve families the relative dualizing complex is a shifted flat module, and it is invertible in the Gorenstein case.

sources.locator: Remark 48.12.5 (0B6S), p. 30; Section 48.28, especially Lemma 48.28.6, pp. 72–75
sources.match: Proper relative duality supplies the normalized complex; rigidity gives uniqueness and base-change compatibility.

sources.locator: Definition 1.1 and discussion of ω, pp. 162–163
sources.match: The pointed stability condition uses the log dualizing line, and the source separates its base-change assertion from the Noetherian duality argument.

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.markingCartier

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.line

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.baseChange

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.mapIso
api.statement: A marking-preserving family isomorphism induces the canonical log-line isomorphism; its composition law lifts scheme cocycles.

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.noetherianComparison
api.statement: On locally Noetherian bases identify ω, its trace, and the marked twist with StableReduction Layer 2 and SF.2/curve-dualizing-comparison.

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.smoothComparison
api.statement: On the relative smooth locus ω identifies with Ω¹_{C/S}; the twist retains the marking divisors.

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.componentDegree

api.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.ample_iff

uses.how: The functorial canonical log line equips scheme descent with an actual lifted polarization cocycle.
Fixed log pluricanonical embeddings and stable-family pullbacks use the same line.
The log line realizes the stability condition and its normalization degree test.

tests.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.rationalThree
tests.statement: Over any field with three distinct chosen points of P¹, L≅O(1), so the family is stable.

tests.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.rationalTwo
tests.statement: For two distinct marks of P¹, L≅O(0); excluding this family prevents mere nonnegative degree from being used for stability.

tests.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.fourPointBoundary
tests.statement: For a two-component stable genus-zero four-pointed fibre split 2+2, log multidegree is (1,1), not (2,2).

tests.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.selfNodeFlags
tests.statement: For an irreducible rational one-nodal curve with one mark, degree is −2+2+1=1, hence stable.

tests.name: PointedCurves.LogDualizing.nonflatBaseChange
tests.statement: For any pointed stable family over k[ε]/(ε²), reduction to k identifies its log line with the fibre log line by the canonical base-change isomorphism.

nodes.title: Geometric realization of the pointed moduli pseudofunctor
nodes.statement: For naturals g,n with 2g−2+n>0 computed in Z, realize StableReductionPartII:key/moduli-curves on all schemes. Start with the category whose objects are an object q:C→S of the native slice category Over S and an ordered n-tuple of slice morphisms from id_S to q; morphisms are slice arrows preserving each of the n sections. Restrict by the actual geometric predicates: proper, flat, finitely presented, nonempty geometrically connected genus-g fibres of pure dimension one, nodality, disjointness and smoothness of the sections, and relative ampleness of the canonical log line. Take the native categorical core of this full subcategory. This is the stable fibre groupoid; its full subgroupoid cut out by smoothness of C→S is the smooth fibre groupoid. Reindex along u:T→S by the native slice pullback and the induced sections. Transport the native slice pullback identity and composition isomorphisms through the pointed full subcategories and their cores to obtain a Pseudofunctor on LocallyDiscrete(Schemeᵒᵖ) with values in Cat and groupoid fibres. The comparisons preserve the ordered marking data and satisfy the unit and pentagon laws. Geometric points recover the groupoid of pointed curves with their full marking-preserving automorphism groups, rather than its set of isomorphism classes.
hypotheses: Fix universes for schemes, fibre categories and the Cat-valued pseudofunctor; use universe enlargement where required.
The geometric predicates refer to the existing StableReduction objects, with arbitrary-base genus and log-duality comparisons above.
There is no assumption that the moduli problem is already algebraic or has a Hilbert atlas.
proofSteps: Use the parent owned definition as the specification and StableReduction Layer 3 as the family and stability interface. Realize sections as actual morphisms in Over S, not named points or unconnected labels.
Use arbitrary-base-genus and arbitrary-base-duality to interpret the family predicates without a locally Noetherian restriction.
On the total curve of a pullback, the i-th section is the unique map with components σ_i∘u and id_T. All geometric conditions are preserved by base change.

Use Over.pullbackId and Over.pullbackComp for canonical comparisons, verify their equations on both projections and all marked sections, and apply Functor.core and Iso.core. These comparison maps give the same coherent pseudofunctor as parent MC.0/pullback-coherence.
Identify arrows in the core with inverse pairs of section-preserving over-S morphisms, and identify geometric fibres with the parent geometric-curve groupoid.
acceptance: A smooth elliptic curve with its origin retains its inversion automorphism in characteristic different from two.
For a fixed ordered triple on P¹, the identity scheme map is not an arrow to a differently ordered triple unless it preserves each label.
A noninvertible section-preserving endomorphism belongs to the ambient pointed slice category when defined, but is not an arrow of the moduli groupoid.

sources.match: Ordered smooth disjoint markings, fibrewise stability and cartesian family isomorphisms specify the geometric fibre categories and their reindexing.
The moduli objects are families over schemes, with base change, and carry a universal family.

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.obj

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.isoEquiv

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.pullback
api.statement: A scheme map induces the actual fibre-product functor on pointed families and isomorphisms.

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.pullbackId
api.statement: The native identity-pullback isomorphism identifies every marking with its original section.

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.pullbackComp
api.statement: The native iterated-pullback comparison preserves every marking and satisfies pentagon and unit laws.

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.smoothInclusion
api.statement: Smooth families form a full subgroupoid, and their inclusion is pseudonatural in the base.

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.geometricPoints

api.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.noetherianComparison

uses.how: Hilbert presentations must present these geometric fibres and their actual isomorphisms.
Forgetful maps, universal evaluation and coarse moduli use the same groupoid rather than classes.
Cartesian arrows determine the category fibred in groupoids.

tests.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.ellipticInvolution
tests.statement: For an elliptic curve E over an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠2, (E,0) is an object at (g,n)=(1,1) and [−1] is a nonidentity automorphism. A set-valued replacement fails this test.

tests.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.orderedTriple
tests.statement: The identity of P¹ is not a marking-preserving map from (0,1,∞) to (1,0,∞); relabelling is not an implicit identification of objects.

tests.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.noninvertibleArrow
tests.statement: In characteristic p>0, the Frobenius endomorphism of P¹ over F_p preserves 0,1,∞ but is not a moduli arrow, since it is not an isomorphism.

tests.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.emptyBase
tests.statement: Over the empty scheme the stable fibre category is equivalent to the terminal groupoid, with empty total curve and uniquely determined marking maps; fibre conditions are vacuous.

tests.name: PointedCurves.Moduli.markingBaseChange
tests.statement: The pullback of each marking is the unique graph map with components σ_i∘u and id_T. Iterated pullback gives the same marking through the native comparison.

nodes.title: Effective descent of the geometric pointed moduli problem
nodes.statement: For an fppf covering of any scheme S, restriction of either the stable or the smooth pointed genus-(g,n) groupoid to its descent-data category is an equivalence. In the stable case, a family isomorphism cocycle induces a specified cocycle of isomorphisms on L=ω(ΣD_i), using rigidity/base-change coherence; this is a lift of the cocycle to line-bundle data, not merely invariance of a line-bundle isomorphism class. Apply polarized descent to obtain a scheme family and descend the marking sections and their equalities. The descended geometric predicates and fixed genus are the ones of native-family-realization. These equivalences give the native Pseudofunctor.IsStack instance for Scheme.fppfTopology and the specified groupoid fibres separately. On the locally Noetherian étale subsite the descended family and log line agree, by a uniquely determined isomorphism compatible with the chosen descent identifications, with the polarized descent already owned by StableReduction Layer 2. The same uniqueness compares with the polarized descent comparison of R09.3 on their common domain.
hypotheses: Use the general polarized fppf descent supplier requested from SF.1, including actual cocycle isomorphisms, arrows and marking maps.
The stable log line is relatively ample by arbitrary-base-duality.
The smooth groupoid is the full subcategory satisfying smoothness, an fppf-local condition.
proofSteps: Use log-duality mapIso and baseChange to lift the curve descent cocycle canonically to L, with its identity and triple-overlap equations.

Use SF.1/space-fppf-descent and SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent through the requested polarized-scheme descent theorem. Relative ampleness is fpqc local, and the descended ample invertible sheaf makes the descended algebraic space a scheme (Stacks 74.13.1).

Descend sections and marking-preserving arrows using the morphism part of the supplier and subcanonicity. Properness, flatness, finite presentation, nodality, geometric connectedness, genus, smoothness/disjointness of markings and log ampleness descend; use Stacks 53.20.9 for nodality.

Translate full faithfulness and essential surjectivity of the descent functor into native IsStack via SF.1/stack-in-groupoids. Preserve automorphisms in this equivalence. Compare étale and fppf descent constructions using full faithfulness, not a chosen equality of objects.
acceptance: For a finite separable splitting cover of a genus-zero three-pointed form, descent recovers the marked curve and its descent identifications. The triviality theorem is imported from MC.2, not used to prove descent.
An elliptic involution in an overlap cocycle descends as actual automorphism data; it is not discarded by passing to classes.
Specifying that a line-bundle class is fixed, without cocycle isomorphisms, is insufficient input to polarized descent.

sources.match: The fppf stack property for polarized proper flat finitely presented schemes follows from space descent, module descent and descent of ampleness.
An ample line descends along fpqc covers, and its existence over a scheme base forces the descended space to be a scheme.

sources.locator: Definition 1.2 and following stack assertion, p. 164
sources.match: The original fibred category and its étale stack assertion motivate the comparison; the fppf and arbitrary-base strengthening uses the Stacks arguments explicitly.

nodes.title: The universal curve represents an unrestricted additional section
nodes.statement: Realize the parent MC.0/universal-curve construction by the pseudofunctor Z̄_{g,n} whose S-objects are stable pointed families (C/S,σ_i) together with any section Δ:S→C, and whose arrows are marking-preserving isomorphisms carrying Δ to Δ. Forgetting Δ defines π:Z̄→M̄. The extra-section pseudofunctor is an fppf stack by effective family descent and descent of section morphisms. For a family x over S, there is a pseudonatural equivalence h_S×_{M̄}Z̄≃h_C over h_S: an object over u:T→S includes a specified isomorphism of its underlying family with u^*x, and that isomorphism carries its extra section to a unique map T→C over S. Thus π is represented by schemes, and its base change along x is exactly f:C→S. It is representable, proper, flat, finitely presented and nodal of pure relative dimension one, with geometrically connected genus-g fibres. Its relative smooth locus is identified under every such base change with that of f; a geometric point is smooth for π exactly when it is smooth in the corresponding geometric curve. The n marking maps M̄→Z̄ send Δ to σ_i. Their images are disjoint and in the relative smooth locus. Δ is otherwise unrestricted and can coincide with a mark or pass through a node; it is not a new stable disjoint marking. No equivalence with M̄_{g,n+1} is assumed; that equivalence is owned by MC.2/expansion-contraction-inverses.
hypotheses: g,n satisfy the stable range and x is an actual object of native-family-realization.
The two-fibre product includes an isomorphism to the fixed pulled-back family.
The representability statement is about the projection, not algebraicity of M̄.
proofSteps: Use the native over-S section Hom description and fibre-product universal property to identify sections of C_T→T with maps T→C over S.

Using SF.1/two-fibre-product, identify an object with a family, an identification with x_T, and an extra section. Transport the section to x_T. The inverse uses x_T with its given section and identity identification.

Prove full faithfulness: an arrow compatible with the fixed identification is uniquely determined. This makes each represented fibre discrete while leaving the automorphisms of Z̄ and M̄ intact. Check pseudonaturality in T and x.
Transport the curve properties through this equivalence and identify the n marking maps. Extra-section descent follows from descent of morphisms; there is no smooth-locus condition on Δ.
acceptance: Over a field the fibre over a pointed curve together with its fixed identification is its entire curve, including every node.
A marking section is itself a valid extra section.
For a curve with automorphisms, discreteness is asserted only after specifying the identification with the fixed family.

sources.locator: Introduction, pp. 1–2, the cartesian universal-family square
sources.match: An extra section has no smoothness or disjointness requirement; applying the construction to the diagonal of C×_S C identifies the pulled-back universal family with C.
The extra-section category is distinct from the stable extra-marking category; expansion and contraction compare them in MC.2.

api.name: PointedCurves.Universal.projectionProperties

Expansion replaces a node or collision by a new component, identifying this universal curve with stable n+1 markings.
Marked clutching and universal sections use the represented curve and its ordered markings.

tests.name: PointedCurves.Universal.collisionAllowed

nodes.title: The smooth-family open and the relative smooth locus
nodes.statement: For a stable family f:C→S, let C_sm be the relative smooth locus, and define S_sm as the open subscheme with underlying set S minus f(|C| minus |C_sm|). The image removed is closed because f is proper. For any u:T→S, the family C_T→T is smooth exactly when u factors through S_sm; the open S_sm and the resulting cartesian square commute with arbitrary base change. Hence the smooth pointed pseudofunctor is a full open subfunctor of the stable one, represented on every scheme test object by S_sm. Pulling the universal curve back to that subfunctor gives C×_S S_sm, with all its markings. This differs from C_sm→S, which keeps smooth points of nodal fibres. Smoothness of the moduli stack over Z, owned by MC.2, is a separate assertion and implies no smoothness of the universal projection over nodal curves.
hypotheses: f is proper, flat and finitely presented with nodal pure-one-dimensional geometric fibres.
The relative smooth locus is taken for f, not for the total space over Z.
proofSteps: Use the native Scheme.Hom.smoothLocus for the relative smooth locus and its base-change characterization. Properness makes the image of its closed complement closed.

The fibre over s is smooth precisely when the entire fibre lies in C_sm. Faithfully flat field extension detects this condition, proving the arbitrary-base-change characterization of the resulting open subscheme.
Apply this construction naturally to every classified family to obtain the represented open subfunctor; identify the restricted universal curve by universal-evaluation.
acceptance: For a smooth family S_sm=S and C_sm=C.
For a stable nodal curve over an algebraically closed field S_sm is empty while C_sm is nonempty.
At a smoothing xy=t, the special fibre contains a nonsmooth node even though the total space may be smooth over the ground field.

sources.match: The smooth-family locus is obtained by removing the proper image of the nonsmooth locus and commutes with arbitrary base change.
Universal evaluation pulls the entire classified curve back; restricting the base to smooth families therefore restricts the whole curve.

requests.need: For proper finitely presented f:X→S over arbitrary schemes, Rf_*E is perfect with arbitrary derived base change if f is flat and E is perfect; likewise for a finitely presented S-flat module. Supply the perfect-complex fibre-amplitude criterion, locally free cohomology in a single fibre degree, and the local splitting induced by O_S→Rf_*O_X when each fibre H⁰ is κ(s). Stacks 36.30.4, 36.32.5 and More on Algebra 15.77.7. The existing derived-pushforward and Tor-independent comparison nodes do not assert this perfection or amplitude conclusion.

Extend the relative-dualizing-module concentration interface to arbitrary-base flat finitely presented Cohen–Macaulay morphisms of pure relative dimension d, using the already owned rigid relative dualizing complex: a pseudo-coherent module flat over the base in degree −d, arbitrary base change, invertibility for Gorenstein fibres, with coherent rigidity and proper trace comparisons. The existing relative-dualizing-module node is restricted to FTS_S with Noetherian S; the curve case is Stacks 109.19.1–109.19.3.

Effective fppf descent for proper flat finitely presented schemes endowed with a relatively ample invertible sheaf and specified compatible cocycle isomorphisms on it. Include morphisms, sections, equalities, refinements and arbitrary base-change compatibility. Recover a scheme from descended algebraic-space and module data using Stacks 74.13.1; cf. 99.14.3. Reuse the same outstanding supplier requested by AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3/r093-polarized-descent-comparison; neither finite-locally-free Galois descent nor StableReduction Layer 2 étale descent supplies this general fppf contract.
Import the already planned relative curve interface: proper flat finite-presentation families and their scheme base change.
Import the already planned nodal/normalization interface, residue dualizing description and branch-count convention, including two branches at a self-node.

Import the existing locally Noetherian coherent genus and trace-normalized relative duality comparisons, log Cartier twists and positivity/relative ampleness criterion, stable-fibre openness and compatibly polarized étale descent. Arbitrary-base and general fppf extensions are exactly the new comparisons and SF requests in this packet.

Import the existing ordered pointed prestable/stable family predicate, smooth disjoint marking sections, marking-preserving arrows, base-change interface and geometric component stability criterion; do not re-own the stable family notion.

sampleExports.contract: The stable and smooth (0,3) groupoids are terminal over Spec Z, with the unique three-point trivialization. This is an MC.2 consequence and not an MC.0 descent prerequisite.
The ordered (0,4) smooth base is P¹ minus 0,1,∞; its stable base is P¹ with the three 2+2 boundary partitions.
Algebraicity, proper Deligne–Mumford structure, smoothness over Z and dimension 3g−3+n are MC.2 conclusions, not assumptions of MC.0.
Universal extra sections correspond to stable n+1 markings via expansion and contraction, with inverse natural family isomorphisms.
Single-mark forgetting followed by stabilization is supplied only when the target pair is in the stable range.

checked.note: Finite diagrams and comparison equations descend by the stated SF.0 suppliers and Stacks 32.10.1–2, 53.20.10; the general-base assertion is affine-local. StableReduction Layers 0–3 supply the existing geometric predicates.
Stacks 53.20.12 and 36.30.4, 36.32.5 support universal H⁰ and locally free R¹. The missing perfection/amplitude supplier remains explicit; no canonical derived splitting is claimed.

Rigid arbitrary-base duality, marking Cartier divisors and component degree give the log line. The SF.2 module-concentration extension remains explicit; tensor/pullback theory is imported from AlgebraicVectorBundles.

Corrected Moduli.obj: the ambient category is ordered pointed slice objects with marking-preserving arrows, then a geometric full subcategory and its core. Checked groupoid fibres, coherence, automorphisms and all five tests.

The canonical log-line isomorphisms lift the cocycle. Scheme effectivity needs the stated polarized supplier, shared with R09.3, rather than an invariant Picard class. Checked Stacks 74.13.1 and 99.14.3.

Added n≥1 to the collision test and narrowed prototype coverage to the four actual slice statements. The geometric two-fibre product, unrestricted extra section, marking recovery and coherent base-change targets remain in the reader.
Properness makes the image of the nonsmooth locus closed; the resulting base open classifies whole smooth fibres, while the relative smooth locus of the stable universal curve can omit nodes.
